reviewPolicy.sourcePolicy: Use only the Element 74 definition for numeric type, maximum length, implied decimals, and purpose; distinguish Element 74 from Standard Message Data Element 99.
reviewPolicy.dataPolicy: Field-level design vectors only. Do not assert that Element 74 is required or decide when the Purchase Card Data Segment applies.
reviewPolicy.baselinePolicy: References BR-RULE-SEG104-R-008 and its placeholder chain; no official Test record is modified.
reviewPolicy.promotionGate: Authorized Test review must confirm Segment 104 applicability, populated-value semantics, full companion fields, encoded fixture, and readiness before promotion or execution.

requirementReferences.title: PC Tax Amount is numeric, up to 7 digits with 2 assumed decimal places, when populated.
PC Tax Amount identifies transaction tax amount in Segment 104.

sourceEvidence.quote: Character Type: N Maximum Length: 7 bytes
sourceEvidence.interpretation: Element 74 is numeric and permits at most seven bytes.

sourceEvidence.quote: Variable length of up to seven digits with two assumed decimal places
sourceEvidence.interpretation: Element 74 has two assumed decimal places; the source does not display a sample value or prescribe the presence condition here.

sourceEvidence.quote: Identifies the transaction tax amount in Data Segment No. 104, Purchase Card Data Segment.
sourceEvidence.interpretation: The element's stated purpose is the transaction tax amount in Segment 104.

sourceEvidence.quote: Note the difference between this data element and Element No. 99, Tax Amount.
sourceEvidence.interpretation: Do not substitute Segment 100 Element 99 or its tax-total semantics for Segment 104 Element 74.

aiReviewReferences.interpretation: All three hash-verified candidate observations declare Element 74 absent; none asserts or observes a PC Tax Amount value. The cases therefore do not demonstrate the amount purpose or its numeric/length constraints.

testScenarios.intent: When Element 74 is populated in an authorized Segment 104 context, check numeric representation, two assumed decimal places, and the seven-digit maximum. Presence and Segment 104 applicability are separate open questions.

testCases.assertion: A five-digit numeric Element 74 value is within the seven-digit maximum; two decimal places are assumed.
A seven-digit numeric Element 74 value is at the documented maximum; two decimal places are assumed.
An eight-digit Element 74 value exceeds the documented seven-digit maximum.
An alphabetic character in Element 74 violates its numeric character type.

openQuestions: Confirm when Segment 104 is applicable and whether Element 74 may be omitted; no presence ruling is inferred from this format draft.
Confirm product/transaction tax semantics and how the assumed decimal places are represented in complete fixtures.
Review the complete candidate payloads and metadata sidecars; the current screen establishes only declared omission, not producer intent or actual wire representation.
Authorize and execute full Segment 104 positive/negative fixtures before promotion.
